overview.description: Every component has a hand-authored <name>.examples.json meant to be a concrete, runnable few-shot reference (correct usage plus anti-patterns) that anchors an agent's generated code to real, verified examples instead of hallucinated training-data patterns. An audit found the corpus split cleanly in two: 12 of 28 files have the full component/examples/antiExamples shape with a props map per example; the other 16 drop antiExamples and props entirely. Three entries were also found to be actively wrong (a literal placeholder, and two using a prop name the real component no longer has) and were fixed directly - see knownFixedDefects below. docs/components/exemplars.json is generated from these files by scripts/generate-component-exemplars.mjs, which normalizes presence (fills in missing antiExamples/props defaults) and validates the result against docs/foundations/component-exemplars.schema.json.
overview.purpose: Give an agent runnable, verified usage code for any component in one place, and make the completeness gap (which components have real anti-pattern guidance vs none) a queryable fact instead of something only discoverable by reading 28 differently-shaped files.

normalizationRules.rule: Defaults to the PascalCase form of the directory id when the source file omits it (12 of 28 files omit it).
normalizationRules.dataInvented: none - this is a mechanical derivation from the directory name, not a guess about content.

normalizationRules.rule: Defaults to an empty array when the source file omits it entirely (16 of 28 files).
normalizationRules.dataInvented: none - an empty array is honest about absence; no anti-pattern is fabricated.

normalizationRules.rule: description defaults to null, props defaults to {} when absent.
normalizationRules.dataInvented: none - missing sub-fields become null/empty, never a guessed value.

exemplarCompleteness.description: Each registry entry gets a structurally-derived exemplarCompleteness: full | partial | thin. full = every example has a non-empty props map AND at least one antiExample exists. thin = no example has a props map AND no antiExample exists. partial = anything in between.
exemplarCompleteness.purpose: Surfaces the real 12-vs-16 completeness split as a queryable signal instead of only living in prose a reader might skip.
exemplarCompleteness.resolution: When a component's examples.json is next substantively touched, add at least one antiExample (a real anti-pattern with a reason, not an invented one) and a props map per example. Same 'migrate when next touched' philosophy as component-api-governance.json's knownViolations and component-registry-governance.json's knownContentGaps - not something to backfill in bulk without real domain review of what's actually wrong for each component.

knownFixedDefects.issue: Two examples used a literal placeholder `onRemove={...}` - not copy-paste runnable.
knownFixedDefects.fix: Replaced with a concrete inline handler (`onRemove={() => handleRemove('filter')}`), matching the corpus's existing convention for self-contained handler examples.

knownFixedDefects.issue: Used `<Checkbox isDisabled>` - Checkbox's real prop (checkbox.tsx) is native `disabled`. This taught a prop that doesn't exist on the component.
One example used `<IconButton ... isDisabled ...>` - IconButton's real prop (icon-button.tsx) is also native `disabled` now.
knownFixedDefects.note: This is the same isDisabled->disabled migration that component-api-governance.json's knownViolations entry and CLAUDE.md still describe as open drift for Button/IconButton - that governance text is itself stale (the migration already happened in source) and is tracked as a separate fix, not part of this artifact.

qualityChecklist.description: A lightweight bar for authoring a new exemplar entry or completing a thin one - not a scored rubric, proportionate to this repo's scale.
items: Real values only - no `{...}`, `TODO`, or truncation. Every jsx string must be copy-paste runnable.
At least one antiExample with a concrete reason - what's wrong and why, not just 'don't do this'.
A props map on every example - the exact prop/value combination the jsx demonstrates.

Verify every prop name against the component's actual current .tsx/.types.ts source, not against component-api-governance.json or CLAUDE.md prose alone - those can go stale (see the Tooltip/Checkbox fixes above, both caused by exactly this).

validationApproach.tool: shared hand-rolled validator: scripts/lib/validate-schema.mjs (extracted from the component-metadata work, reused here rather than duplicated)
validationApproach.revisitThreshold: Add a real JSON Schema library (e.g. ajv) only if a schema needs features the mini-interpreter doesn't support (oneOf, $ref, conditional if/then) - not before.

generation.rationale: Same convention as docs/components/registry.json and packages/ui/src/tokens/generated - committed generated output, regenerated on demand, not auto-run or staleness-checked in CI (matching the existing npm run generate:icons precedent).
